title: Fractions on a {{term:number-line}}
summary: Fractions are numbers too, and each one has its own place on the number line. Split the space from 0 to 1 into equal parts and place points.
guide: On a {{term:number-line}}, numbers get bigger from left to right: 0 is on the left and 1 is to its right.
The space from 0 to 1 is one whole. The small marks split it into equal parts. If there are 4 parts, each part is {{frac:1/4}}, and three parts along from 0 you reach {{frac:3/4}}.
Tap the line to place a point. You can drag a point, or tap it and move it with the arrow keys. A point always lands on the nearest small mark.

Some fractions are bigger than 1, like {{frac:5/4}}. These are called {{term:improper-fraction}}s. {{frac:5/4}} is one whole and another {{frac:1/4}}. Written as {{mixed:1 1/4}}, it is called a {{term:mixed-number}}.

engine.label-line: Number line: tap to place a point

three-quarters.title: Three quarters on the line
three-quarters.prompt: The space from 0 to 1 is split into 4 equal parts. First predict: is {{frac:3/4}} nearer to 0 or to 1? Then place a point on {{frac:3/4}}.
three-quarters.hint: Each part is {{frac:1/4}}. Start at 0 and move 3 parts to the right.
three-quarters.success: Well done! You moved three quarters along from 0 and reached {{frac:3/4}}.
three-quarters.why: Why is {{frac:3/4}} nearer to 1 than to 0?
three-quarters.model: Because from {{frac:3/4}} to 1 there is only one part left, {{frac:1/4}}. But from 0 to {{frac:3/4}} there are three parts.

feedback.count: Place one point on the line. Just tap the line.
feedback.too-big: Your point has gone too far. Move just 3 parts along from 0.
feedback.too-small: Go a little further. You need to move 3 equal parts along from 0.

thirds.title: One third and two thirds
thirds.prompt: This time the space from 0 to 1 is split into 3 equal parts. Place two points: one on {{frac:1/3}} and one on {{frac:2/3}}.
thirds.hint: Each part is {{frac:1/3}}. The first small mark after 0 is {{frac:1/3}} and the second is {{frac:2/3}}.
thirds.success: Great! {{frac:1/3}} and {{frac:2/3}} are both in the right place.
thirds.why: How many times as far from 0 is {{frac:2/3}} as {{frac:1/3}}? Use the line to explain.
thirds.model: Twice as far. {{frac:2/3}} is two lots of {{frac:1/3}}. To reach {{frac:1/3}} you move one part, and to reach {{frac:2/3}} you move two equal parts.

feedback.count: There must be exactly two points on the line: one for {{frac:1/3}} and one for {{frac:2/3}}.
feedback.wrong: At least one point is in the wrong place. Count the parts from 0: one, two.

five-quarters.title: More than one
five-quarters.prompt: Now the line goes from 0 to 2, and each whole has 4 equal parts. Predict: does {{frac:5/4}} come before 1 or after it? Then place a point on {{frac:5/4}}.
five-quarters.hint: {{frac:4/4}} is the same as 1. Move one more part past 1.
five-quarters.success: That's right! {{frac:5/4}} is just past 1: one whole and another {{frac:1/4}}.
five-quarters.why: {{frac:5/4}} is an {{term:improper-fraction}}. How can you tell it is bigger than 1?
five-quarters.model: Its numerator (5) is bigger than its denominator (4). Four quarters make one whole, with one {{frac:1/4}} left over. So {{frac:5/4}} is the same as {{mixed:1 1/4}}.

feedback.count: Place one point on the line.
feedback.too-small: You haven't reached {{frac:5/4}} yet. First go to 1 (that is {{frac:4/4}}), then one more part.
feedback.too-big: Too far. {{frac:5/4}} is just one part past 1.

read-mixed.title: Read a mixed number
read-mixed.prompt: The line goes from 0 to 3, and each whole has 3 equal parts. What number does the point on the line show? Write it as a {{term:mixed-number}}: the whole number in the left box and the fraction beside it.
read-mixed.hint: First see which whole number the point comes after. Then count how many parts past that number it is.
read-mixed.success: Well done! The point is at {{mixed:2 1/3}}: two wholes and {{frac:1/3}}.
read-mixed.why: {{mixed:2 1/3}} can also be written as a single fraction. What is its numerator, and why?
read-mixed.model: 7, so it is {{frac:7/3}}. Each whole has 3 parts, so two wholes are 6 parts. One more part makes 7 parts: seven thirds.

feedback.empty: Write the whole number, the numerator and the denominator.
feedback.too-small: Your number is smaller than the point. Don't forget to count the wholes before the point.
feedback.too-big: Your number is bigger than the point. Check which whole number the point comes after, and how many parts past it it is.
feedback.wrong-denominator: Each whole on this line has 3 equal parts, so the denominator is 3.
feedback.zero-denominator: The denominator can't be 0. How many parts does each whole have?
feedback.not-mixed: Right amount, but write it as a mixed number: the whole number in the side box and the leftover fraction.
